title: The horosphere discrimination: a signed Busemann level set instead of a distance
equation: L_horo = -log softmax_j( -|b_xi(q_j) - b_xi(s_i)| / T ) [j = label_i], with xi the target's hyperbolic position as the base point, b_xi the Busemann function of that base point, q_j the level-0 codewords, s_i the source's hyperbolic position, and label_i the codeword the host's own assignment gives the target

symbols.b_xi: the Busemann function of the base point xi in the Poincare ball of curvature -c; its level sets are the horospheres centred at xi, and those level sets are Euclidean spheres in the ball whose centre is xi/(1 - c|xi|^2), which is NOT the centre of the hyperbolic sphere of the same radius
symbols.xi: the base point: the TARGET's hyperbolic position, detached, so the term moves the codebook and not the encoder
symbols.s_i: the SOURCE's hyperbolic position; the horosphere through it is the level b_xi(s_i)
symbols.q_j: the level-0 codewords, mapped into the ball with the same expmap0 and tangent scale as the latents
symbols.T: the temperature, locked at specification time at 0.25

behaviour_signal: the train-split transition pair: the source item and its successor, read only from the train split
codebook_interaction: the level-0 codeword the host assigns to the target is pulled onto the horosphere through the source and the other codewords are pushed off it; the label is the host's own assignment, detached, so it does not move with the term
encoder_interaction: none: the base point and the source level are detached, so the term moves the codebook and the export, and leaves the encoder's gradient exactly as the host left it
basepoints: the target's hyperbolic position, used as the base point of the Busemann function
risk: the horosphere is a global level set: if the codewords spread along the level instead of across it, the term separates the level-0 codes without improving the successor's code, and the arm collapses to a use-based split that the ER gate would not catch
falsifier: the exported level-0 usage does not change, or the level-0 usage collapses onto fewer codes than the control, or the arm's ER does not exceed the control's 16.38953942232631
why_not_the_measured_failures: the four measured failures are a gyro-translation (R8-07), a Frechet barycentre of the successors (R8-08), a per-layer radial hierarchy (R8-09) and a graph-code Gromov-Wasserstein (R8-10). None of them is a signed level set: the horosphere compares the SIGNED Busemann levels of the codewords with the level of the horosphere through the source, and the sign is what distinguishes the inside of the horosphere from the outside. A gyro-translation moves the points; a barycentre averages them; a hierarchy reweights the layers; a Wasserstein matches the graphs. This term does none of those: it asks which side of a horosphere a codeword is on.
why_not_just_euclidean: the matched Euclidean twin keeps the same code and replaces the Busemann level with the squared Euclidean distance to the base point. The constraint is therefore not the same one: the horosphere's level sets are Euclidean spheres centred at xi/(1 - c|xi|^2), while the distance's spheres are centred elsewhere, so the codeword each constraint selects is not the same codeword. The arms hyp_horosphere_c1 and eucl_horosphere_c1 are the pair, and the ER difference between them is the evidence that the double-curvature geometry is what does the work
literature_evidence: the identifiers were retrieved from Crossref and arXiv on 2026-10-23 and are recorded in results/hyperbolic_research_runs/literature/ with the request and the response; the access level is verified_abstract_only, so no equation is claimed from their full text

mechanism.summary: the level-0 codeword of the target belongs to the horosphere through the source, measured with the signed Busemann level
